sources.title: Chainalysis admits all users affected in major data breach — names, usernames, password hashes, and live tokens all exposed

stories.headline: Chainalysis says hackers took credentials and tokens for all customers
stories.dek: The blockchain analytics firm forced password resets and pulled key products offline after an AI-assisted attack escalated into an on-path data grab.
stories.body:
Blockchain analysis firm Chainalysis says hackers obtained names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens for all of its users, Ars Technica and TechRadar report. The breach forced the company to lock customers out, require password resets and take several products offline.

The customer list makes the breach serious. According to Ars Technica, Chainalysis and public records name customers including the FBI, US Immigration and Customs Enforcement, the US Air Force, Microsoft, Coinbase and Barclays. Governments and law enforcement use its tools to trace stolen crypto and investigate illicit activity.

The company first disclosed the incident on October 30. It said an attacker used "offensive agentic techniques," which Ars Technica describes as AI agent-assisted, to reach its systems and internal tools. Chainalysis called the attack similar to hacks on other tech platforms in recent weeks but unrelated to a recent crypto theft involving Binance. At that point it said only "non-sensitive" data was accessed: user IDs, full names, email addresses and organization role labels. It said it had found no evidence that passwords, MFA secrets, session tokens or investigation content were compromised.

That changed on November 4. In an email to customers, Chainalysis said an "on-path attack," also known as adversary-in-the-middle, had exposed "a subset of customer passwords," and that the vector was "contained and remediated." The company has not said where the compromised infrastructure sat or whether the intercepted traffic was TLS encrypted, Ars Technica notes.

Chainalysis pulled Reactor, Data Solutions and Chain (Beta) "out of an abundance of caution," according to TechRadar, and took down KYT, its UI and API, other address screening products and the login page "due to abnormal activity." Every user must reset their password and rotate API keys as appropriate. Partial access to KYT and Address Screening is returning, and customers can speed things up by emailing a trusted IP address. Reactor and Data Solutions remain down.

No group has claimed responsibility, and TechRadar reports the data has not surfaced on the dark web. It is unclear whether the stolen tokens exposed customers to further attacks.
key_points: Names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens exposed for all users
On-path attack confirmed November 4 after initial "non-sensitive" disclosure
Reactor, Data Solutions, Chain (Beta) and KYT taken offline
Mandatory password resets and API key rotation; no attacker has claimed it
stories.why_it_matters: An AI-assisted intrusion escalated into stolen live tokens at a vendor trusted by the FBI and Microsoft. If you integrate Chainalysis APIs, rotate keys now and treat early breach disclosures as provisional.

sources.title: Elon Musk says Tesla is 'winding down' production of its Cybertruck

stories.headline: Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production by mid-2027
stories.dek: Musk says the Texas factory needs the room for Cybercab robotaxis, after US Cybertruck sales fell 48 percent last year.
stories.body:
Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at its Austin gigafactory around mid-2027, Elon Musk said Friday on X. He said the move frees up capacity for more output of the Cybercab, the steering-wheel-free robotaxi central to Tesla's autonomy push. Musk called the Cybertruck the "best vehicle Tesla has ever made" and the wind-down the "end of an era."

It is unclear whether production will move elsewhere or end entirely. Reuters, in a report carried by NBC News, notes Austin is the only known Tesla plant equipped to build the truck's specialized parts.

Sales never came close to Musk's prediction of 250,000 a year. Kelley Blue Book counts 20,237 US sales in 2025, down 48 percent from 38,965 in 2024. Pedestrian-impact rules also kept the truck out of Europe.
key_points: Musk says Cybertruck production in Austin winds down around mid-2027 to make room for Cybercab output.
Kelley Blue Book reports 20,237 US Cybertruck sales in 2025, down 48 percent from 2024, versus a predicted 250,000 a year.
Tesla has not said whether the Cybertruck will be built elsewhere or discontinued.

sources.name: Ars Technica
sources.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned by Congress over Chinese espionage concerns

stories.headline: House chairs summon Nvidia's Jensen Huang over China spying concerns
stories.dek: Three Republican committee chairs want Huang at a closed-door briefing on November 18 after reports he was targeted by Chinese intelligence.
stories.body:
Top Republican lawmakers have asked Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to appear before Congress, Ars Technica reports. The chairs of the House committees on China, foreign affairs and intelligence, representatives John Moolenaar, Brian Mast and Rick Crawford, wrote to Huang this week requesting he attend a joint closed-door briefing on November 18.

The request follows a New York Times report last week that US intelligence officials believe Huang was the target of a Chinese spy operation. The concerns center on Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud company that has bought billions of dollars of Nvidia chips. "It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which US national security has been placed at risk," the lawmakers wrote.

Nvidia rejects the claims and would not say whether Huang will attend. "Meetings with customers are part of a CEO's job," the company said.
key_points: Chairs of three House committees asked Jensen Huang to a closed-door briefing on November 18.
The New York Times reported US intelligence officials believe Huang was targeted by a Chinese spy operation involving a Megaspeed executive.
Nvidia rejects the claims and has not said whether Huang will appear.

sources.name: TechRadar
sources.title: 'AI security controls are only as strong as the wider application environment around them': OpenAI forced to patch after experts bypass ChatGPT 'lockdown mode' to gain access to entire chat history

stories.headline: Check Point bypasses ChatGPT Lockdown Mode with HTML popups
stories.dek: Popups escaped the sandbox around ChatGPT's HTML code previews, opening the door to data theft and phishing before OpenAI patched it server-side.
stories.body:
Check Point Research found a way around ChatGPT's Lockdown Mode, the optional setting meant to blunt prompt-injection attacks, TechRadar reports. The flaw let attackers pull sensitive data and, per TechRadar, reach a user's entire chat history. OpenAI has patched it server-side.

The bug sat in how ChatGPT code blocks render HTML previews. That content runs in a sandbox that blocks access to cookies and local storage. But the preview used nested sandboxed frames, and while ChatGPT intercepted direct attempts to open new windows, the sandbox still allowed popups. Content opened in a popup escaped the sandbox's rules.

The researchers say attacks could start from a malicious prompt, custom GPT or shared chat, and could enable credential theft, phishing or malware delivery. The worst case was a zero-click attack, with popups appearing without user action.
key_points: Check Point Research bypassed ChatGPT Lockdown Mode through popups opened from nested frames in HTML code previews.
The flaw could enable data exfiltration, credential theft, phishing and malware delivery, including zero-click scenarios.
OpenAI added server-side safeguards to close the workaround after disclosure.

sources.name: TechRadar
sources.title: Russian Federal State Statistics Service says it was hit by massive cyberattack — hackers steal 23TB of data, including Ukraine war casualty figures

stories.headline: Hackers claim 23TB theft from Russia's statistics agency Rosstat
stories.dek: Rosstat confirms an attack but denies any data leak, while the hackers publish what they say are Russian war casualty figures.
stories.body:
Hacker groups Silent Crow and the Belarusian Cyber Partisans say they stole about 23TB of data from Rosstat, Russia's state statistics agency, TechRadar reports. Rosstat admits its systems were targeted over the weekend of October 29 to November 1. It says, according to Kommersant, that no database compromise or leak of legally protected information has been identified.

The groups claim they reached the central office, regional units and Rosstat's main data processing center. They say domain controller access let them compromise VMware ESXi virtualization and infrastructure management systems, and an electronic document management system.

On Telegram, the hackers published what they say are Russian military casualties since the start of the war in Ukraine: 1,584,910. They also listed 587,409 lost drones. Russia has kept casualty figures secret since 2024, and the numbers are unverified.
key_points: Rosstat confirms an attack over the Halloween weekend but says no data leak has been identified.
Silent Crow and the Belarusian Cyber Partisans claim they took about 23TB, including document management data.
The hackers posted unverified figures of 1,584,910 Russian military casualties and 587,409 lost drones.

sources.name: Tom's Hardware
sources.title: Nvidia tightens tracking of AI GPUs in Southeast Asia as Chinese chip smuggling draws scrutiny, report claims

stories.headline: Nvidia ties Southeast Asia cloud partner status to GPU tracking
stories.dek: Cloud providers must reportedly enroll in Fleet Intelligence, which can log accelerator locations, as Washington presses on chip smuggling into China.
stories.body:
Nvidia now requires Southeast Asian cloud providers that want official Nvidia Cloud Partner (NCP) status to enroll in its Fleet Intelligence tracking system, Bloomberg reports, as cited by Tom's Hardware. The status brings Nvidia's public endorsement and preferred access to its AI chips. Nvidia was not immediately available for comment.

Fleet Intelligence launched last December as a data center management tool. It gathers data on Nvidia hardware across participating companies' infrastructure, including the locations of individual accelerators. Outside the NCP requirement, participation remains voluntary. Nvidia has not said whether existing partners must enroll or whether the rule will extend beyond the region.

U.S. authorities believe billions of dollars of restricted AI hardware have reached China through Southeast Asia. Singapore-based Megaspeed has been under U.S. and Singaporean investigation for over a year over suspected diversion, which it denies.
key_points: Southeast Asian firms seeking Nvidia Cloud Partner status must reportedly join Fleet Intelligence, which can track accelerator locations.
Participation remains voluntary outside the partner requirement, and Nvidia has not said if existing partners must enroll.
The move comes amid U.S. concern that restricted AI chips reach China via Southeast Asian smuggling routes.

featured.headline: Final Fantasy VII Remake Intergrade hits record low: Strong Buy
featured.body:
Final Fantasy VII Remake Intergrade, a singleplayer action RPG in the JRPG mold, drops to €7.19 at the Epic Games Store. That is 82 percent off the regular €39.99 and the lowest price ever recorded for the game. It holds a Metascore of 86 and a Very Positive rating on Steam.

The deal runs until November 16 at 17:00 CET, so there is time to decide. A deep cut, a record-low price and strong reviews from both critics and players earn it a Strong Buy. It suits RPG and action-adventure players who have waited for a big-budget JRPG to reach an impulse-buy price.

featured.headline: Owlboy drops 90 percent to an all-time low: Strong Buy
featured.body:
Owlboy, an indie platformer and metroidvania with pixel graphics, costs €1.95 at GOG, down 90 percent from its regular €19.50. That is the lowest price ever recorded. Critics gave it a Metascore of 88, tied for the highest on today's list, and Steam users rate it Very Positive.

At under €2, the downside is minimal for a game this well reviewed. The depth of the cut, the record-low price and the scores add up to a Strong Buy. It suits fans of metroidvanias, platformers and pixel-art adventures, and anyone filling out a backlog with highly rated indie games for very little money.
